rationale: yoga_layout rebuilt the entire YGNode tree on every layout pass -- YGConfigNew, YGNodeNewWithConfig per view, a full style walk, solve, then YGNodeFreeRecursive -- so every node looked new to Yoga on every pass. That defeated Yoga's own optimizations by construction: dirty-subtree skipping never applied because nothing was ever clean, and the per-node measure cache was discarded before it could be hit. The dominant cost was throwing the solver's state away, not the solve. This change retains the node tree across passes and reuses it when the view tree's shape is unchanged. Two hazards come with reuse and both are handled explicitly. Conditional style writers that skip zero or unset values are correct against a fresh node and wrong against a reused one, where the previous value survives the skip; styles are now written unconditionally into a pristine thread_local scratch node reset with YGNodeReset and copied across with a single YGNodeCopyStyle, so a cleared property actually clears. Measure caches go stale when a leaf's intrinsic size or label text changes without its style changing; a MeasureSignature over the bit-compared intrinsic width and height plus a hash of the label text re-dirties the node when it moves, and measure funcs are cleared when a leaf loses its intrinsic size or gains children. The retained UI kernel is touched at core/view/src/yoga_layout.cpp; core/view/src/widget_bridge/layout_api.cpp gains static trace scopes only. No public signature, no measure-func contract, and no layout result changes -- the same tree produces the same geometry, which is what the widened yoga test suite asserts. This is Pulp-only: the rebuild-every-pass shape is an artifact of how Pulp owns its view tree, and a Vellum-native retained UI kernel should derive node lifetime from its own tree-identity model rather than copy Pulp's shape-signature and scratch-node handshake. Measured at 3-4x faster per layout pass with roughly 5x fewer allocations and 83 percent node reuse against 0 percent before. It is deliberately not claimed as a user-visible speedup: in the Spectr frame that motivated the investigation, layout is about 3 percent of the run and the end-to-end A/B delta sat inside run-to-run variance. There is no named immutable Vellum framework commit to backport against, and this records no Vellum acknowledgement.
